title: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (Artificial Intelligence Act), incl. consolidated version 02024R1689-20260727
issuer: European Parliament and Council of the EU
license_or_reuse_terms: EUR-Lex reuse with attribution (Commission Decision 2011/833/EU); only OJ text authentic. Not re-checked.

relevant_provisions.paraphrase: Bans placing on the market, putting into service or using AI to infer emotions of people in workplace and education institutions, except for medical or safety reasons.
relevant_provisions.relevance_to_adhd_app: School/employer deployment inferring attention or frustration from biometrics is likely prohibited unless medical; consumer self-use is outside.

relevant_provisions.paraphrase: Bans manipulative/deceptive techniques and exploitation of vulnerabilities due to age, disability or socio-economic situation that materially distort behaviour and cause significant harm.
relevant_provisions.relevance_to_adhd_app: Reward loops or nudges exploiting impulsivity (e.g., to drive purchases) risk this ban. Commission guidelines C(2025) 884 para. 105 give as a prohibited example a game that gives children personalised, unpredictable rewards through addictive reinforcement schedules, where it causes significant harm.

relevant_provisions.paraphrase: Emotion recognition means inferring emotions or intentions from biometric data; physical states such as pain or fatigue are excluded.
relevant_provisions.relevance_to_adhd_app: Whether 'attention' is an emotion or a cognitive/physical state decides applicability. Commission guidelines para. 240 and 255 treat inferring learners' attention or interest as emotion recognition; fatigue stays excluded (para. 249, 261).

relevant_provisions.paraphrase: Certain emotion recognition and education AI is high-risk, requiring transparency and effective human oversight including override.
relevant_provisions.relevance_to_adhd_app: Education or emotion-recognition variants become high-risk from 2 Dec 2027 (post-Omnibus).

relevant_provisions.paraphrase: Deployers of emotion recognition systems must inform exposed persons.
relevant_provisions.relevance_to_adhd_app: Tell users when physiological signals are used to infer affective states.

title: Digital Omnibus on AI — Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 amending the AI Act
issuer: European Parliament and Council of the EU
license_or_reuse_terms: Official text not opened; CSA note is third-party — cite, do not copy.

relevant_provisions.paraphrase: Published in OJ 24 July 2026, in force 27 July 2026; Annex III high-risk deferred to 2 Dec 2027, Annex I to 2 Aug 2028, Art. 50(2) watermarking for existing systems to 2 Dec 2026.
relevant_provisions.relevance_to_adhd_app: Extra runway for any high-risk variant; prohibitions and Art. 50 disclosure still apply now.

title: Commission Guidelines on prohibited AI practices under Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (C(2025) 884 final)

relevant_provisions.paraphrase: An education institution using emotion recognition to infer students' interest and attention is a prohibited example (para. 255); gaze tracking that only records fixation points without inferring emotions is not prohibited (para. 255); fatigue detection for pilots/drivers is not emotion recognition (para. 249, 261). The medical exception is narrow: therapeutic use means CE-marked medical devices, general wellbeing monitoring is not covered (para. 256-257), while assisting students with autism can qualify (para. 263).
relevant_provisions.relevance_to_adhd_app: Directly maps onto attention-state monitoring; avoid institutional deployment. A wellness-claim app cannot rely on the medical exception.

relevant_provisions.paraphrase: Covers inference of emotions and intentions, but only on the basis of biometric data (para. 244-245, 250). Biometric data includes behavioural biometrics such as keystrokes (way of typing), eye tracking and heartbeats (para. 251); inferring emotions from written text is outside (para. 251, 265).
relevant_provisions.relevance_to_adhd_app: Gaze, HRV/EDA and keystroke dynamics are biometric; typed content sentiment is not. The guidelines do not say whether task-performance data (missed items, reaction-time variability) counts as behavioural biometrics.

title: Regulation (EU) 2016/679 — General Data Protection Regulation
issuer: European Parliament and Council of the EU
license_or_reuse_terms: EUR-Lex reuse (attribution). Page opened; article text not rendered in fetch.

relevant_provisions.paraphrase: Prohibits processing health data and identifying biometric data unless an exception such as explicit consent applies.
relevant_provisions.relevance_to_adhd_app: HRV/EDA-derived attention or stress states in an ADHD context are very likely health data; explicit granular consent needed. Note Art. 9(1) covers biometric data only when processed for uniquely identifying a person.

relevant_provisions.paraphrase: Child consent for online services valid from 16 (Member States may lower to 13); below that parental authorisation is required.
relevant_provisions.relevance_to_adhd_app: Younger students need verifiable parental consent.

relevant_provisions.paraphrase: Limits solely automated decisions with significant effects; DPIA required for high-risk processing such as large-scale special-category data.
relevant_provisions.relevance_to_adhd_app: DPIA effectively mandatory.

title: Age appropriate design: a code of practice for online services (Children's Code)
license_or_reuse_terms: ICO usually Open Government Licence v3.0 (unverified); PDF is a third-party mirror — ico.org.uk original NOT opened.

relevant_provisions.paraphrase: No nudges leading children to give unnecessary data or weaken privacy protections.
relevant_provisions.relevance_to_adhd_app: Rewards must never unlock extra sensor permissions or sharing.

relevant_provisions.paraphrase: Best interests of the child, DPIA, no detrimental data use, high-privacy defaults, profiling off by default.
relevant_provisions.relevance_to_adhd_app: Attention profiling of under-18s off by default.

relevant_provisions.paraphrase: A secondary source says children's protection was embedded in UK GDPR Art. 25(1) from 19 June 2025.
relevant_provisions.relevance_to_adhd_app: Would make child-centred design statutory; NOT verified on legislation.gov.uk.

title: Children's Online Privacy Protection Rule, 16 CFR Part 312 — 2025 amendments (eCFR source note: 78 FR 4008, Jan. 17, 2013, as amended at 90 FR 16977, Apr. 22, 2025)
license_or_reuse_terms: US federal text public domain. Checked against eCFR text up to date as of 6 Nov 2026 (authoritative but unofficial); Federal Register original not opened.

relevant_provisions.paraphrase: Adds biometric identifiers usable for automated recognition, e.g. fingerprints, iris/retina, voiceprints, gait patterns, facial templates, genetic data.
relevant_provisions.relevance_to_adhd_app: Gait/motion and face templates from under-13s covered; HRV/EDA not named. COPPA covers children under 13 only (§312.2 'Child'), so a 13-17-year-old user is outside it.

relevant_provisions.paraphrase: Parents must be able to consent to collection and use without consenting to disclosure to third parties, unless disclosure is integral to the service, and the operator must obtain separate verifiable parental consent to such disclosure (§312.5(a)(2)); data may not be retained indefinitely and a written retention policy must state purposes, business need and a deletion timeframe (§312.10); data collected for internal operations may not be used for behavioral advertising or to amass a profile on a specific individual (§312.2). Compliance date 22 April 2026 as reported, not shown in eCFR.
relevant_provisions.relevance_to_adhd_app: No ad/analytics SDK sharing without separate consent; inferred-state profiles must not feed behavioral ads; define deletion schedules. Applies to under-13s only.

title: Federal Decree-Law No. (45) of 2021 Concerning the Protection of Personal Data
issuer: United Arab Emirates (UAE Data Office as regulator)
license_or_reuse_terms: No open licence found — link rather than copy.

relevant_provisions.paraphrase: Excludes health personal data governed by its own legislation and free zones with their own data laws.
relevant_provisions.relevance_to_adhd_app: If treated as health data, UAE health-data law may apply instead; DIFC/ADGM hosting changes regime.

relevant_provisions.paraphrase: Cabinet to issue Executive Regulations within six months.
relevant_provisions.relevance_to_adhd_app: 2026 secondary sources (Chambers 2026, uaeexperthub) say still unissued, so breach timelines, DPO thresholds and fines remain unclear.

relevant_provisions.paraphrase: Sensitive data includes health, biometric and genetic data; processing generally needs consent subject to exceptions.
relevant_provisions.relevance_to_adhd_app: Treat physiological/attention data as sensitive.

title: Law No. (13) of 2016 on Protecting Personal Data Privacy (PDPPL)
issuer: State of Qatar (NCSA / National Cyber Governance and Assurance Affairs)
license_or_reuse_terms: Official Arabic on Al Meezan not opened; translations hosted by third parties — cite only.

relevant_provisions.paraphrase: Data on ethnic origin, children, health, physical or psychological condition, religion, marital relations and criminal offences is 'special nature' data, processable only with permission from the competent department.
relevant_provisions.relevance_to_adhd_app: Attention/stress/ADHD data and any child data need an NCSA permit in addition to consent.

relevant_provisions.paraphrase: Child-directed website operators must give notice, obtain explicit guardian consent and not condition participation on unnecessary data.
relevant_provisions.relevance_to_adhd_app: Student versions need guardian consent and minimisation.

title: Privacy Notice — Guidelines for Regulated Entities (PDPPL-02050213E v2.0)

relevant_provisions.paraphrase: Confirms children's data is special-nature and expects child-directed notices that highlight special-nature processing.
relevant_provisions.relevance_to_adhd_app: Notices must flag physiological data in child-readable form.

title: Personal Data Protection Law (Royal Decree M/19, as amended) and Implementing Regulation
license_or_reuse_terms: Not stated; seen by research subagent only.

relevant_provisions.relevance_to_adhd_app: GCC rollout needs DPO and 72-hour breach process; effective date reported inconsistently (14 Sep vs 17 Oct 2023).

title: Law No. (30) of 2018 with respect to Personal Data Protection

relevant_provisions.relevance_to_adhd_app: Applies to Bahraini users; sensitive-data clauses NOT verified.

title: MDCG 2019-11 rev.1 — Qualification and classification of software (MDR 2017/745, IVDR 2017/746)
issuer: Medical Device Coordination Group / European Commission
license_or_reuse_terms: Commission reuse policy; MDR text not opened.

relevant_provisions.paraphrase: Software is medical device software based on intended purpose (e.g., diagnosis, monitoring, treatment or alleviation of disease or disability), regardless of platform.
relevant_provisions.relevance_to_adhd_app: 'Helps manage ADHD' claims can make the app MDSW; 'study habits' claims less likely.

relevant_provisions.paraphrase: Software informing diagnostic/therapeutic decisions is at least Class IIa, other MDSW generally Class I; rev.1 (June 2025) clarified intended purpose and modules.
relevant_provisions.relevance_to_adhd_app: Modular design can keep wellness modules outside MDR.

relevant_provisions.paraphrase: June 2025 FAQ on interplay between MDR/IVDR and the AI Act.
relevant_provisions.relevance_to_adhd_app: Notified-body MDSW makes its AI high-risk via AI Act Art. 6(1), now from 2 Aug 2028.

title: General Wellness: Policy for Low Risk Devices (January 2026)
license_or_reuse_terms: US government work, generally public domain.

relevant_provisions.paraphrase: Low-risk (non-invasive, non-implanted) products intended only for general wellness fall under enforcement discretion; issued 6 Jan 2026, superseding 2019.
relevant_provisions.relevance_to_adhd_app: Non-invasive HRV/EDA/motion wearables with focus/stress wellness claims can stay outside device oversight.

relevant_provisions.paraphrase: Claims to diagnose or treat a specific disease fall outside the policy.
relevant_provisions.relevance_to_adhd_app: 'ADHD management' claims probably exceed it; not verified clause-by-clause.

title: Software as a Medical Device: Possible Framework for Risk Categorization (IMDRF/SaMD WG/N12FINAL:2014)

relevant_provisions.paraphrase: Categories I–IV by significance of information (treat/diagnose, drive or inform clinical management) against healthcare situation (critical, serious, non-serious).
relevant_provisions.relevance_to_adhd_app: A medical ADHD tool that informs management of a non-serious condition would be lowest category. NOT opened.

title: Characterization Considerations for Medical Device Software and Software-Specific Risk (IMDRF/SaMD WG/N81 FINAL:2025)

relevant_provisions.paraphrase: Published 29 Jan 2025; complements N12, stresses clear intended purpose and direct and indirect harms.
relevant_provisions.relevance_to_adhd_app: Indirect harms such as anxiety from false 'distracted' alerts belong in the risk file.

title: Guidelines on measures to ensure a high level of privacy, safety and security for minors online, Art. 28(4) Regulation (EU) 2022/2065 (C/2025/5519)

relevant_provisions.paraphrase: Minors should not be exposed to persuasive design features aimed predominantly at engagement that may lead to overuse (Section 6.4, Online interface design), nor to manipulative design techniques such as scarcity, intermittent or random rewards, or to paid loot boxes with random outcomes, that can lead to excessive or unwanted spending or addictive behaviour (Section 6.6, Commercial practices, para. 69(k)-(l)).
relevant_provisions.relevance_to_adhd_app: Variable-ratio rewards collide with this; use predictable user-set rewards.

relevant_provisions.paraphrase: Push notifications should be off by default for minors and always off during core sleep hours (para. 57(b)(vii)); streaks, autoplay and similar excessive-use features disabled by default (para. 57(b)(vi), (viii)).
relevant_provisions.relevance_to_adhd_app: Break prompts for minors should be opt-in, if the app is an 'online platform' (uncertain).
